comment: The decisive comparison was D versus B: AdamW with beta2=.999 beat coupled Adam with beta2=.95. I implicitly favored faster second-moment adaptation without supporting evidence. Longer averaging could stabilize noisy minibatch updates, while coupled decay changes Adam’s adaptive moments; the revealed ranking cannot isolate either mechanism. Backtesting found no matched historical XOR comparison of these full recipes. Across nine matched-network/rate historical comparisons in other families, AdamW won six and lost three. One beta-only lab XOR comparison favored .999 (.31168 versus .37598 CE), but used 16 features and 1024 steps, outside this regime. K1002/K1003/K1070 helped order the other choices; K1005 warned against precisely this unsupported tie-break. No general rule is established.
